findings.note: CODE-ONLY FIX - no row I can author is safe. The two branch conditions print are BOTH two-skill conditions ("already trained in ONE of these skills", "trained in BOTH skills") and the only per-option gate the choice lane has is SkillRankGate (types.ts:2817), which names exactly ONE skill. Gating the existing two options on their own skill being untrained would empty the picker for a character trained in both - the failure mode narrowChoiceOptions' own doc calls worse than an over-wide list. The feat half cannot be data either: a FEAT's choice.options[].grant.grantsFeats is NOT read (build.ts:5406/5465 collect that lane for heritage and classFeature effectChoices only, and the comment at build.ts:5400 says so outright - "Heritage options only; applyAlwaysOn has no feat arm"), which is exactly why the pairing lives in src/rules/featFeatGrants.ts CHOICE_FEAT_GRANTS today. Both halves are listed in CROSS-FILE GAPS.

CODE-ONLY FIX. The wrong free skill is src/rules/featGrantsAuto.ts:474 `'intuitive-crafting': { skills: { crafting: 'trained' }, redundantFallback: true }`; redundantFallback is a FeatGrant field whose only reader is build.ts:5829 and it fires whenever the static skills map is redundant - i.e. for the MIDDLE case as well as the both-already-held one. The record itself carries no choice and no skill lane, so there is no data field to correct: an effect-backfill row would have to ADD a second carrier on top of the src one and double the grant. The one-line fix is in CROSS-FILE GAPS.

CODE-ONLY FIX. The borrowing lane the proposal names is FeatGrant.armorFamiliarity {armors, rank, mirrorBest} (src/rules/featGrants.ts:310), whose ONLY writer of Proficiencies.armorOverrides is build.ts:5806/7082 reading grantsFor(featId) - a src registry. No item field and no record field feeds armorOverrides, so the item-side attachment the finding asks for cannot be authored as data. I deliberately did NOT emit the note-removal row either: dropping "set it yourself" before the lane lands leaves the player with neither the number nor the instruction. Both rows are listed under DATA STILL NEEDED, to be authored in the same batch as the src entry.

Note also that feats/hardwood-armor grants TWO items, hardwood-armor-armor and hardwood-armor-shield; only the armour takes the borrowing. See CROSS-FILE GAPS and DATA STILL NEEDED.

Built on the EXISTING automaton enhancement lane rather than a new one: Feat.enhancement (types.ts:3359, EnhancementDef) is the payload a record only HAS while an augmentation names it, and enhancement.choiceIds names which of the record's own effectChoices the tier switches on (build.ts:6334-6345 filters them out for any automaton whose augmentation has not picked this feat). That is exactly the proposal's "switched on ONLY when an augmentation feat that names Hardened Chassis is held", and it needs no reader of its own. The chosen-type branch reads the record's OWN base answer through onlyWhenFlag {flag:'hardenedChassisDamage'} (types.ts:2074, honoured by effectChoiceOptions at build.ts:1633 so the picker and resolvePick agree), so it is three flag-gated options rather than a second question. Half-your-level-minimum-3 is the string-formula form IwrEntry.value already takes (types.ts:482; max(1,floor(@actor.level/2)) etc. already ship). FOUR options, never one - build.ts:6347 warns that a one-option effectChoices picker is auto-applied by resolvePick and would deliver the tier unconditionally; with any flag answer at least two options survive the onlyWhenFlag filter. VERIFIER: the two augmentation picker notes are re-emitted here with supersedes:true — without them the sheet computes the tier while the picker still says it does not, which is the Q27 state this lane exists to end.

findings.note: CODE-ONLY FIX. The collection is not a record field at all: archetype/flexible-spellcaster carries nothing but id/name/edition/aonId, and the shape comes from ClassArchetype.spellCollection (types.ts:1666) whose entire implementation is the branch at build.ts:4475 - it walks slotCounts PER RANK and writes entry.slots[rank] / entry.repertoire[rank], with Builder.tsx:367/387 mirroring it. Turning that into one flat pool sized by the TOTAL daily class slots (with a one-1st-rank-spell floor) is engine work in those two files; no backfill row can reach it. Listed in CROSS-FILE GAPS.

The proposal's own shape - "let the feat hand over a small feature carrying the second daily-preparations question" - because a record has exactly ONE choice def and haunting-memories' is already the proficiency pick. The carrier is a category:'bonus' feat (the established grant-only shape: 14 such records ship and featSlots.ts:140 keeps category 'bonus' out of every picker), handed over by the feat's own grantsFeats, which build.ts:5410 reads for every taken feat and which lands the carrier in c.feats - the set ownedDailyChoiceRecords (derive.ts:1294) walks for daily questions. The question itself is the EXISTING wizard lane the proposal names: choice.kind 'open' + from.type 'feat' + from.grantFeat (types.ts:2202, Experimental Spellshaping), whose answer dailyChoiceGrants turns into a real day-long grantsFeats at derive.ts:1820. The half-level cap is from.maxLevelByLevel (featsMatching, openChoice.ts:53), NOT WG's flat level 10: base 4 at levels 8-9, then one step per two levels to 10 at 20th. The printed "minimum requirement of your new rank in the chosen skill" is a prerequisite-TEXT restriction nothing can filter on, so it is choice.note - the field dailyChoicesFor already renders beside the morning row.

choice.prompt: Haunting Memories — this morning's borrowed skill feat
choice.note: It must be a skill feat whose minimum requirement is the rank you raised your chosen skill to this morning — the app cannot filter on prerequisite text, so that half is yours to honour. The list is already capped at half your level, as print requires for its level prerequisite. The feat lasts until your next daily preparations, so it can't be a prerequisite for a permanent character option.
